# ColorMap

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Editing` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public sealed class ColorMap : IEditSurface<Rgba32>
```

Editable single-layer raster storing full-color RGBA, bound to a fixed canvas size — the color-mode counterpart to [`ValueMap`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ValueMap.md), and the only surface a Custom layer's artwork can be painted on. It deliberately mirrors the value-map's shape ([`ColorMap.ForCanvas()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ColorMap.md#m-forcanvas-nfty-core-model-dimensions), [`ColorMap.Clone()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ColorMap.md#m-clone), [`ColorMap.ToImage()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ColorMap.md#m-toimage), [`ColorMap.FromImage()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ColorMap.md#m-fromimage-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixlabors-imagesh-b045ce), a bounds-tolerant [`ColorMap.Set()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ColorMap.md#m-set-system-int32-system-int32-sixlabors-imagesharp-pix-a93c82)) so the paint stack treats the two identically. Materialize an `Image` only at export/preview.

### FromValueMap(ValueMap) { #m-fromvaluemap-nfty-core-editing-valuemap }

```csharp
public static ColorMap FromValueMap(ValueMap map);
```

Lifts a grayscale value-map into color: each pixel becomes `(v, v, v, a)`, exactly what [`ValueMap.ToImage()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ValueMap.md#m-toimage) writes. This is what an author sees the instant they switch a Dynamic or Static layer into color mode — the drawing they already have, in gray, ready to be painted over. Switching the palette must never alter a pixel, so this is a widening and not a recoloring: no hue, no saturation, no colorization is consulted.

**Parameters**

- `map` (`ValueMap`) - The value-map to widen.

**Returns.** A new color map with the same dimensions and the same visible pixels.
